title: Looking back
hookLine: stories, practices, portions, sayings, tales and songs: a year of Jewish life
tomorrow: year one close: the big lookout
last: LET EVERY THING THAT HATH BREATH PRAISE THE LORD.

cards: Scroll back far enough through the photos on a phone and something odd happens. A plate of food. A street corner.

A friend's face mid-laugh. Each one was just a Tuesday when it was taken. Laid end to end, they turn into a story: here's where things changed, here's the week that went badly, here's the morning it got better.
A list of ordinary moments becomes a map. The Torah keeps a list like that. Today, one for a year of Jewish life.

teach.b: Near the end of the Book of Numbers, just before the Israelites reach the promised land, the Torah stops and lists every place they camped in the wilderness, one name after another. It could look like a boring list.
But Rashi, the great commentator, passes on a parable. A king's son was sick, and his father took him far away to be healed.

teach.h: HERE WE SLEPT, HERE WE WERE COLD.
teach.b: On the way home, the father pointed out each place: here we slept, here we were cold, here you had a headache. The list is love. Every stop counted.
First words: shalom, the Shema, Shabbat, bracha, tzedakah, teshuvah. The stories: creation, Abraham, Jacob's long road, Joseph, the Exodus, the sea, Sinai.
The practices: Shabbat candles, blessings through the day, the holidays as they came, tefillin, kashrut, study as prayer. The text, one portion at a time, from Bereshit into Exodus.
Then the depths: the sayings of Pirkei Avot, be a mensch, don't judge until you've been there. A taste of Talmud: Hillel on one foot, Honi and his carob tree, these and these.

The Hasidic tales: the shepherd boy's whistle, Zusya, the narrow bridge, the rebbe with the axe. And the Psalms, all the way to neshamah, breath and soul. Some days on this path were missed, some half heard.
The Torah's list keeps the hard stops too: Rephidim, it says, where there was no water for the people to drink.

how: The portion Masei, read once a year in the weekly cycle, lists all the Israelites' stops in the wilderness, and many Jews use the weeks before Rosh Hashanah to look back over the year that has passed.

o: naming each stop on the road, hard ones too
wishing you could go back to the start
fixing every mistake made along the way

games.q: the Israelites are about to enter the promised land after forty years. what does the Torah do first?
o: stop and list every place they camped.
tell them to forget the wilderness.
games.why: Numbers 33 lists every stop. Rashi's parable: a father on the way home points out each place. here we slept, here we were cold.

practice: Let the year play back without trying to remember everything, until five things come up that stayed with you: a word, a story, a practice you actually do now, a line you've said to someone else, a moment that changed how you see something.
Count them on your fingers, one by one, and if you have paper nearby, write them down afterward. If you pray, give thanks for each one.

wordCard.voice: Looking back. The Torah stops before the promised land to name every place the people camped. Here we slept. Here we were cold. Every stop counted.

orig.note: Hebrew: the journeys of. The name of the portion that lists the wilderness stops (Numbers 33).

carryVoice: Your line: look how far. Every stop counted, even the dry ones. One day left in year one.
